newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigeria exposes political asylum ring.
newsitem.headline: Nigeria exposes political asylum ring.

text.p: Nigeria warned the world on Wednesday of a group called United Front for the Liberation of Nigeria (UNFLN), which it said specialised in seeking political asylum abroad with forged documents.

"The aim of membership is to secure political asylum overseas under false pretences," said army spokesman Lieutenant-Colonel Felix Chukwumah, while parading before reporters five UNFLN members he said had tried to enter South Africa as political refugees.
Military-ruled Nigeria is shunned by many powerful countries including South Africa for lack of democracy and alleged human rights abuses.
But these countries have also frequently complained of bogus asylum seekers from Nigeria who turn up on their borders falsely claiming to be victims of political persecution.

Chukwuma alleged that Gbadebo Alade (28), Oladele Abimbola (27), Temitope Bamidele (25), Shehu Isiaka (25) and Yinusa Ogedengbe (27) stowed away from Douala port in Cameroon in a Liberian registered ship, M.V. Seagull Fortune early this year.
Armed with documents purporting them to be members of the opposition National Democratic Coalition (NADECO) group, their aim was to disembark in Durban, South Africa to seek asylum, he said
They were discovered when the ship docked in Equatorial Guinea and were handed over to the Nigerian embassy there, which repatriated them to the country on January 18.
"Before this last attempt they had employed various means to win the sympathy required to secure political asylum in Germany," said Chukwumah.
He said the five men, who did not speak to the reporters, would be released to their families.
Nigeria has been in turmoil since the military annulled democratic elections in 1993, triggering riots and strikes.
